key_insight: A neural-network surrogate boundary condition improves local neutron transport modeling by approximating particles returning from surrounding geometry.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can iterate tokamak port-plug designs without repeated full-model transport or component-to-global mesh joining.
method: Train a neural network to reproduce the component boundary response from surrounding geometry.
Run Monte Carlo transport only within the component, using the surrogate to approximate returning particles.
Compare local flux predictions with global transport and vacuum or reflective boundary approximations.
evidence_signal: In a simplified benchmark geometry, surrogate port-plug flux differed by less than 12% from global transport in every energy bin, outperforming vacuum and reflective boundaries in accuracy while running faster than global transport.
watch_item: Accuracy and speed gains require validation for realistic tokamak geometries and design changes beyond the demonstrated benchmark.
paper_title: A Surrogate Boundary Condition for Improved Accuracy and Performance of Local Modeling in Radiation Transport Simulations
